y: The stress is on the last part: COME.
a: Overcame moves the same way: o-ver-CAME!
q: Where is the stress in overcome?
s: Save this and practice it.

y: Americans stress TISE, like in advertise.
a: British speakers say ad-VER-tis-ment!
e: I saw an advertisement for jobs.
q: Where is the American stress in advertisement?
s: Save this and say it out loud.

y: In letter words, stress the last letter.
a: Same with DVD and CEO!
e: Is there an ATM near here?
q: Where is the stress in ATM?
s: Save this before you need cash.

y: Here the strong part is CHECK.
a: The verb is check out, two words!
q: Where is the stress in self-checkout?
s: Save this for your next shopping trip.

y: Furthermore already means and. Don't add and.
a: It sounds formal. In chat, say also!
e: The hotel is clean. Furthermore, it's cheap.
q: The plan is safe. ___, it saves money.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: He admitted to break the vase.
y: Admit plus -ing means say you did it.
a: Admit to breaking it is also correct!
s: Send this to a snack thief.

r: I'll make up for being late.
y: Make up for means do something good after a problem.
a: Dinner is a classic way to make up for things!
e: Let me make up for it with dinner.
Nothing can make up for lost time.
m: MAKE UP FOR = fix it with something good
q: I'll buy lunch to make up ___ the delay.
The phrase is make up for.
s: Send this to someone who owes you.

w: I wish I can speak French.
r: I wish I could speak French.
y: Wish is about unreal things, so use could.
a: Wish moves the verb back in time!
e: I wish I had more time.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

w: The tour was didactic. Loved it!
r: The tour was instructive. Loved it!
y: Instructive is positive. Didactic can sound preachy.
a: Didactic often means teaching too much!
e: The guide gave an instructive talk.
m: good learning = INSTRUCTIVE, too much teaching = DIDACTIC
s: Save this for your next review.

w: Can I borrow from the other library loan?
r: Can I get it through interlibrary loan?
y: Interlibrary loan brings books from other libraries.
a: It's often free for students!
e: I ordered the book by interlibrary loan.
q: The book is not here. Try ___ loan.
s: Save this for your next research paper.

y: Stress the part before -tion: TEN.
a: Every -tion word follows this rule!
q: Where is the stress in detention?
s: Save this for your next shipping call.

y: Suspicious of means you don't trust it.
a: Be careful with suspicious emails!
e: She was suspicious of the price.
s: Send this to a friend who clicks links.

w: Money is not the problem. Time it is.
r: It's time that is the problem, not money.
y: It is X that shows the most important part.
a: Great for strong answers in interviews!
e: It was my mom who called.
q: ___ the price that I don't like.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

y: The order is fixed: thick and thin.
a: It means in good and bad times!
e: Friends stay through thick and thin.
They stayed together through thick and thin.
m: THICK and THIN = good and bad times
q: Real friends stay through thick and ___.
The idiom is through thick and thin.
s: Send this to your best friend.

r: Cashback means I get some money back.
y: Cashback returns money after you buy.
a: In some stores, cashback also means taking cash at the till!
e: This card gives two percent cashback.
s: Save this before you shop.

w: We are committed to reduce waste.
r: We are committed to reducing waste.
y: Here to is a preposition, so use -ing.
a: Same with look forward to seeing you!
e: She is committed to helping kids.
q: The company is committed to ___ prices low.
s: Save this for your next essay.

y: Their means belonging to them.
a: There, their, they're sound the same!
s: Send this to a confused friend.

w: A guest made a problem talk.
r: We got a guest complaint about noise.
y: When a guest is unhappy, it's a guest complaint.
a: Good hotels answer complaints within hours!
e: The manager handled the guest complaint.
We had three guest complaints today.
s: Save this for your hotel job.

y: The strong part is CROWD.
a: The main word gets the stress!
q: Where is the stress in overcrowded?
s: Save this for your next trip.

w: I'm tired. Moreover, can you pass the salt?
r: The room is small. Moreover, it's noisy.
y: Moreover adds a stronger point. It's formal.
a: Don't use it in casual chat!
e: The car is old. Moreover, it's unsafe.
q: The job pays well. ___, it's close to home.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I don't dare to saying it.
y: Dare plus base verb, or dare to plus verb.
a: How dare you! is a strong, angry phrase!
s: Save this if you dare!

w: Can you replace me tomorrow at work?
r: Can you cover for me tomorrow?
y: Cover for means do someone's work while they're away.
a: Cover for can also mean hide someone's mistake!
e: I covered for Maria last week.
q: I'm sick. Can you cover ___ me?
s: Send this to your work buddy.

r: Utilities are water, gas and electricity.
y: In housing, utilities are home services you pay for.
a: Rent often doesn't include utilities!
e: Utilities cost me 100 dollars a month.
Are utilities included in the rent?
s: Save this before you rent a place.

y: The verb lack takes no of.
a: The noun uses of: a lack of sleep!
q: The verb lack takes no of.
s: Save this for your next essay.

y: Further means more. Farther is distance.
a: Further works for distance too!
e: The station is farther than I thought.
Do you have any further questions?
s: Save this for your next email.

y: Contactless means you tap your card or phone.
a: Most people just say: can I tap?
q: Just tap your card. It's ___ payment.
s: Save this for your next coffee run.

y: Stress the part before -tion: JEC.
a: In daily US talk, people say shot!
e: The nurse gave me an injection.
q: Where is the stress in injection?
s: Save this for your next doctor visit.

w: I can't concentrate in my work.
r: I can't concentrate on my work.
y: Concentrate on means give all your attention to.
a: Focus on works the same way!
e: I need to concentrate on my exam.
s: Save this for exam season.

y: Hesitate is followed by to plus verb.
a: This line ends lots of work emails!
s: Save this for your next work email.

w: Phones are 60 percent of our sales.
r: Phones account for 60 percent of our sales.
y: Account for means make up an amount.
a: It can also mean explain: account for the delay!
e: Rent accounts for half my pay.
Young people account for most users.
s: Save this for your next report.

y: Rarely is already negative. No don't.
a: Hardly and seldom work the same way!
q: Rarely already has a negative meaning.
s: Send this to a friend who rarely texts.

w: Give me a detailed bill, please.
r: Can I get an itemized bill?
y: Itemized means every item is listed alone.
a: Detailed is more general. Itemized is line by line!
e: The hotel sent an itemized receipt.
q: A bill that lists every item is ___.
s: Save this before you check out.

w: I need a magnet photo of my knee.
r: I need an MRI of my knee.
y: Magnetic resonance imaging is called an MRI.
a: No radiation, just big magnets!
e: The doctor ordered magnetic resonance imaging.
q: MRI uses magnets and radio waves.
s: Save this for your next doctor visit.

w: I'm vegetarian, so I eat fish.
r: I'm vegetarian, so I don't eat meat or fish.
y: Vegetarians eat no meat and no fish.
a: Vegans also skip eggs and milk!
s: Save this for your next dinner order.

y: The strong part is THE.
a: It sounds like an-es-THEE-zhuh!
q: Where is the stress in anesthesia?
s: Save this for your next hospital visit.

w: I congratulate you for your new job.
r: I congratulate you on your new job.
y: Congratulate someone on a success.
a: Congratulations on works the same way!
e: We congratulated her on the award.
s: Send this to someone who just won.

w: I wish it doesn't rain tomorrow.
r: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
y: For the future, use hope, not wish.
a: I wish it would stop raining shows you're annoyed!
q: For possible future things, use hope.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: The problem comes out of bad planning.
r: The problem stems from bad planning.
y: Stem from means is caused by.
a: Like a plant growing from a stem!
e: Her fear stems from a car crash.
m: STEM FROM = grows from a cause
q: The delay stemmed ___ a computer error.
s: Save this for your next essay.

y: Feel like plus -ing.
a: Here like works like a preposition!
e: Do you feel like going out?
s: Send this to a sleepy friend.

y: You steal things. You rob people or places.
a: Thieves rob a bank and steal the money!
m: STEAL a thing, ROB a person/place
s: Save this and keep your phone safe.

y: The property manager runs the building for the owner.
a: The landlord owns it. The manager runs it!
e: The property manager fixed the heat.
Email the property manager about repairs.
s: Save this before you rent.

w: Water is a luxury. I need it.
r: A sports car is a luxury.
y: A luxury is nice and costly but not needed.
a: A hot bath can feel like a luxury!
e: Eating out is a luxury for us.
q: For many people, a private jet is a ___.
Something costly and not needed is a luxury.
s: Save this and treat yourself.

y: Words ending in -ic: stress just before it.
a: Same with fantastic and economic!
q: Where is the stress in organic?
s: Save this for your next grocery trip.

y: Fond of means you like someone warmly.
a: It's softer than love!
s: Send this to someone you're fond of.

w: Don't risk to lose your money.
y: The verb risk takes -ing.
a: The noun takes of: the risk of losing!
e: I won't risk missing the bus.
s: Save this before you invest.

w: I'm keeping money for a new laptop.
r: I'm saving up for a new laptop.
y: Save up means keep money over time for something.
a: Save up for plus the thing you want!
e: She's saving up for a car.
We saved up for our trip.
q: I'm saving ___ for a new phone.
The phrase is save up for.
s: Save this and start saving up!

r: The flood caused a lot of damage.
y: Damage, meaning harm, has no plural.
a: Damages with -s means money a court orders!
e: Was there any damage to the car?
q: The fire caused a lot of ___.
s: Save this for your next report.

y: Whose asks who owns it. Who's means who is.
a: Same sound, very different meaning!
s: Send this to a friend who writes who's.

y: Impulse buying means buying without planning.
a: Stores put candy near the till for this!
e: Online sales lead to impulse buying.
q: Buying things you don't plan to buy is ___ buying.
s: Send this to your shopping buddy.

y: A qualification is an official record of your skills.
a: Degrees and certificates are qualifications!
q: An official record of study is a qualification.
s: Save this for your next job form.

y: The stress is on the first part.
a: Many Americans say LUG-zhuh-ree!
e: A spa day is a luxury.
q: Where is the stress in luxury?
s: Save this and say it like a pro.

y: Nevertheless means but we still did it.
a: It's a formal way to say still!
e: It was late. Nevertheless, she called.
The test was hard. Nevertheless, I passed.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I wonder where is the bank.
r: I wonder where the bank is.
y: After I wonder, use normal order: where it is.
a: Same with I don't know where it is!
e: I wonder what time it is.
q: Use normal order after I wonder.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: Want to play together this weekend?
r: Want to hang out this weekend?
y: Adults say hang out, not play.
a: Kids play. Adults hang out!
e: We hung out at the beach.
q: Hang out is natural for adults.
s: Send this to your best friend.

y: Resemble needs no word after it.
a: Also never say is resembling!
s: Send this to someone who looks like you.
